comments.body:
🤖 **Hero BF16 4K update (September 23).** Explicit `<|eot_id|>` stopping in the diagnostic H100 vLLM producer ended 29/32 GSM8K responses before the 4K cap; 3 still hit it. All 32 matched the earlier run token-for-token until the new stop. Eight had the required final `####` line, and five were correct. The earlier “32/32 length-capped” result came from a producer with no effective EOS (`skip_tokenizer_init=True`); it does not establish production SkyRL stopping behavior.

At the pinned step-108000 BF16 export, 128 H100s scored all 32 saved trajectories with full-prefix captured routes. The table covers **29 stopped responses, 3,334 distinct response tokens**. Gaps are absolute selected-token log-probability differences at fixed weights; the ratio count is outside `[0.8, 1.2]`.

| Same-token comparison | Mean gap | p99 | Max | Ratio count |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Megatron route replay vs sampled vLLM | 0.004997 | 0.050673 | 0.120830 | 0 |
| vLLM full-prefix prefill vs sampled vLLM | 0.011993 | 0.133770 | 0.339922 | 9 |

The three length-capped responses contributed 11,751 more tokens and two Megatron/sampled-vLLM ratios above 1.2. Same-input serving prefill changed the top token at 19/3,334 stopped positions. This is a serving execution-shape effect at the same weights, not evidence that Megatron alone causes the residual.

A focused 619-token, four-response learner probe used exact-final-line rewards `[1, 0, 1, 0]`. One `behavior_clip` update took 115.9 s; captured-route hit and executed-set match were 1.0, PPO clipping was zero, full-model hashes changed on all 128 ranks, router gradients were nonzero, and frozen query-bias hashes stayed equal. Batch shape alone changed pre-update Megatron scores by up to 0.0721, so the earlier mixed-shape readback was not a clean update measure; the focused run measured before and after on the *same batch*. This proves an observable reward-derived update, not learning quality or sustained RL throughput. It used one response from each of four different prompts, so it does not exercise grouped GRPO, weight publication, or staleness. The older zero log-ratio checks remain Megatron self-consistency checks, not vLLM agreement.

**Decision:** H100 is **NO-GO for current-checkpoint RL qualification**: the matched numerical sample uses step 108000, and a normal grouped update, weight-version sync, and sustained iteration timing remain untested. GB200 is **NO-GO / untested**: the known 64-GB200 layout cannot safely place on the spare rack while another 64-GPU job is scheduling-gated. The inspected current Hero checkpoint line reaches permanent step 144000, but no matching BF16 serving export was found in the inspected roots. Next: export the current permanent checkpoint to BF16 serving weights; run matched tokens, weights, and executed routes plus a grouped 32×4 update with publication/readback and sustained timing on H100, then repeat on GB200 when the spare rack is safely available. Propose an RL acceptance rule for Romain's approval before any GO; the old Levanter gate remains unchanged.

**Candidate RL gate for Romain's approval:** on each accelerator at a matched current BF16 export, use production-shape 32×4 grouped rollouts; require full captured-route hit and executed-set match, and at most 0.1% sampled-vLLM-versus-Megatron fixed-weight ratios outside the behavior-clip band `[0.8,1.2]` across *all trained response tokens*, with stopped, capped, and reward-valid subsets reported separately. Then verify a finite grouped update, frozen query bias, router-weight change, weight-version publication/readback, and at least ten end-to-end iterations at configured sync/staleness, reporting latency and peak memory. The H100 diagnostic's 2/15,085 out-of-band ratios motivate the proposed band, but do not satisfy the remaining conditions or constitute approval.

<details><summary>Jobs, exact sources, and reports</summary>

- H100 serving stop: `/hero-vllm/hero-vllm-qualification-6716ff937517`, `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/romain/hero-4k-closure-01a0bca4/h100-eot-7755aaca7/`.
- H100 same-input serving prefill: `/hero-vllm/hero-vllm-qualification-39383e7619cc`, `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/romain/hero-4k-closure-01a0bca4/h100-eot-full-prefill-6259b62b6/`. Iris ended `worker_failed` after a pod deletion, but all 32 complete rank JSON and route files had already been uploaded and validated. Diagnostic source: [vLLM branch](https://github.com/yonromai/vllm/tree/goal/hero-4k-eot-stop-01a0bca4), head `6259b62b6608fd25ceadbccd61b3f9f16ccf8617`.

🤖 H100 progress, 26 September. The current Hero run passes the numerical gate; the learning and sizing conclusions remain provisional.

The independent fixed-weight bank has 50,962 response tokens. Replaying routes leaves 5 ratios outside `[0.8, 1.2]` (0.00981%, below the 0.1% limit); native routes leave 114 (0.22370%). The first four grouped updates have actual PPO clipping of 0%, 0.000353%, 0.001180% and 0%. Executed routes and selected publication readbacks match exactly, all router biases stay frozen, and admitted staleness stays within one version. This is MarinSkyRL `fa7059545a8a6ec62456fda3bdb9ce05dae103f8` with vLLM `25f0fc1aae71cccb6da65046cff13145512a6946`, BF16, TP1, fresh MuonH/AdamH/Adam state.

Hero starts at **563/1,024 correct held-out answers**. Later evaluations are pending. The matched Snowball control rose from 823/1,024 to 970/1,024 at version 64: +14.36 percentage points, paired bootstrap 95% interval +12.01 to +16.70. Snowball used its earlier qualified runtime (`80259a0b`); its gain does not establish Hero's gain.

Matched learner measurements use the same 128 sequences and 116,351 prompt-plus-response tokens, one optimizer update per step, and four steps with the first profiled step excluded:

| Model | H100s | PP/EP/CP | Warm update time | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| Snowball | 8 | 2/4/1 | 36.5–45.8 s | Smallest stable tested; 90% CPU AdamW offload, 1,333 GiB host peak |
| Snowball | 16 | 2/8/1 | 12.6–13.1 s | 50% CPU AdamW offload |
| Snowball | 32 | 2/8/1 | 5.53–5.64 s | Best tested throughput per GPU |
| Snowball | 64 | 2/8/1 | 3.43–3.61 s | Diminishing returns above 32 |
| Hero | 96 | 24/4/1 | 19.7–20.2 s | Smallest stable tested; 75.04 GiB peak GPU allocation |

Hero's 96-GPU PP12/EP8 alternative failed the second backward pass. The best 72-GPU resident-memory bound exceeds physical H100 memory. Hero 96 costs about 10.8 times the GPU-seconds of Snowball 32 for this bank; the 128-GPU Hero comparison is queued.

Snowball serving on eight H100s reaches 7,279 / 12,275 / 19,502 response tokens/s at 256 / 512 / 1,024 concurrent requests, with no KV preemption. These are native counter deltas in a supplied portion of an 8,192-request workload, using non-eager BF16, batch invariance, `max_num_seqs=128` and `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`. Throughput is still rising. Larger batches at 1,024/2,048 requests and Hero's 24-GPU sweep are running.

In Hero's integrated run, warm training takes 19–25 seconds but weight sync takes 193–195 seconds, including about 19 seconds of verification readback and 7 seconds of optimizer offload. Publication and barriers need to be accounted for before recommending a larger serving fleet.

Evidence is under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/romain/hero-learning-01a0dca4/`: `h100-learning-a5/report.json`, `hero-learner-h100-96g-a2/report.json`, `snowball-learner-h100-{8g-a4,16g-a2,32g-a1,64g-a1}/report.json`, and `snowball-capacity-h100-a5/report.json`. Primary Iris jobs are `/romain/hero-learning-h100-01a0dca4-a5`, `/romain/hero-learner-h100-96g-01a0dca4-a2`, and `/romain/snowball-capacity-h100-01a0dca4-a5`. Raw evaluations, inputs, counters and native traces are retained beside those reports.

Open gates: Hero held-out gains on both accelerators, full GB200 restore followed by a grouped update, serving knees and fleet balance, controlled TIM costs, and the final High-tier GOAL review. PR readiness remains gated on that review.

🤖 **First Hero held-out gain on H100; later evaluations are running.** On the same 1,024 GSM8K questions, Hero rises from **563 correct at version 0 to 585 at version 16** (54.98% → 57.13%). The paired gain is **+2.15 percentage points**, with a pointwise 95% bootstrap interval of **+0.29 to +4.00**: 56 answers improve and 34 regress. Both evaluations have 12 length-capped responses. Question IDs, prompt tokens and reward rules match the Snowball control exactly.

Version 16 has exact selected-weight/all-router-bias publication readback, changed trainable weights and frozen router biases. Its full MuonH checkpoint saved successfully in 984.81 seconds. The current job continues to version 32, with a planned restore and continuation to versions 48/64; this first positive point does not close the learning-curve gate. Source remains `fa7059545a8a6ec62456fda3bdb9ce05dae103f8`, vLLM `25f0fc1aae71cccb6da65046cff13145512a6946`, on 128 learner + 24 serving H100s. The earlier comment records the passing 50,962-token numerical gate and first four normal updates.

**Snowball serving now has a measured H100 operating point.** With eight H100s, non-eager BF16, TP1/EP8, batch invariance and 4,096 batched tokens per engine:

| Client concurrency | Max sequences per engine | Supplied decode tokens/s | Decode tokens/GPU/s | Concurrent prefill tokens/s | Max KV use | KV preemptions in supplied window |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2,048 | 512 | 25,254 | 3,157 | 4,996 | 45.8% | 0 |
| 4,096 | 512 | 32,770 | 4,096 | 6,432 | 87.1% | 0 |
| 4,096 | 1,024 | 32,967 | 4,121 | 7,426 | 75.6% | 0 |
| 8,192 | 1,024 | 29,061 | 3,633 | 5,502 | 100% | 9,712 |

Concurrency 4,096 is the best tested point: throughput rises below it and falls 11.8% when concurrency doubles. Mean TTFT increases from 2.16 to 24.98 seconds at 8,192. Rates use native cumulative counters while replacement requests remain available, excluding startup and final drain. The final two points have four full concurrency waves; earlier points have eight. Intermediate concurrencies were not measured, so this is not an exact optimum.

Hero's 24-H100 serving fleet also reaches a concrete KV limit: concurrency 384 gives 1,739 supplied decode tokens/s, 420 KV preemptions in the supplied window and mean TTFT 34.08 seconds. The 32-H100 comparison is still running. These serving measurements use the same fixed prompt/forced-response-length mix, with actual combined lengths 244–4,041 tokens, mean 916.

The integrated Hero run remains inefficient at this small group batch. Over updates 4–15, median cycle time is 428 seconds: about 29 seconds in the complete training phase, 195 seconds in weight sync/readback and 201 seconds waiting for groups. Its 16 generation workers permit a nominal 128 responses in flight, much less concurrency than the serving capacity sweep. Fleet recommendations must account for batch size, staleness and publication cadence.

The final H100 gain is +4.59 percentage points, paired 95% bootstrap interval [2.54, 6.64]. GB200 gains +5.47 points [3.61, 7.32], with 78 questions improving and 22 regressing. These intervals measure question-sampling uncertainty, not variation across training seeds. Repeating the same step-32 checkpoint changes the net score by +3 answers on H100 and −3 on GB200. On GB200, 30 answers improve and 33 regress in that repeat, with 256 response sequences changing. One repeat pair per accelerator does not estimate the full distribution of runtime variation.

Independent decoding reproduces all 12,288 retained evaluation rewards across the two curves. The pinned rule requires natural completion and a standalone final `#### number` line; length-capped responses receive zero. GB200 version 64 has 20 length stops versus 13 at baseline. These are exact-answer results under that rule, which can reject mathematically correct responses with the wrong format. The task uses the same held-out question IDs, dataset bytes, tokenizer and prompt template as the control. The analyzer checks prompt lengths and dataset metadata; it does not retain and compare full prompt-token arrays.

The qualified path is BF16, TP1, at most 4,096 prompt-plus-response tokens, separate same-accelerator learner and serving fleets, and actual generation overlapping policy training. Fresh RL uses new MuonH/AdamH/Adam state at rates 1e-6; resume restores the RL optimizer. Query-balancing biases stay frozen. The H100 learning continuation uses 128 learner GPUs (PP16/EP8/CP2) and 24 serving GPUs. GB200 uses 48 learner GPUs (PP12/EP4/CP4) and 16 serving GPUs.

The current fixed-weight checks cover 50,059 response tokens on the final H100 sizing trial and 54,090 on the GB200 continuation. Route replay leaves 6 and 5 ratios outside [0.8, 1.2], respectively: 0.01199% and 0.00924%, below the 0.1% qualification limit. Native routes fail that limit on both backends, so replay remains required. Every resumed GB200 update has exact executed-route checks and sampled learner/serving readbacks, frozen biases and staleness at most one. Maximum observed PPO clipping is 0.17554%, below the 1% per-update gate. At update 58, six of seven bounded weight samples change; the ShortConv K sample is unchanged, while its serving readback still matches. The other 31 resumed updates change all seven samples.

GB200 restores step 32 in 1,384.12 seconds. All 48 optimizer ranks and 384 groups retain their expected state layout; populated Adam/AdamH counters reach 64. Momentum-only groups have no scalar step field. All 42,292 bounded tensor samples are finite. The final checkpoint saves in 961.59 seconds: 5,362,110,400,395 bytes across 60 objects. Its completion markers identify step 64, and all 206,958 DCP storage ranges fit their 48 shard objects. These checks establish metadata completeness and sampled state agreement; they are not full-byte optimizer checksums. Iris reports 16/16 tasks succeeded, zero failures or preemptions, for `/romain/hero-learning-gb200-01a0dca4-a3`.

The last H100 sizing trial, `/romain/hero-integrated-h100-01a0dca4-a8`, also finished: 20/20 tasks succeeded. Its 128-learner/32-serving layout, batch 512 × eight responses and disabled profiler pass all six updates. Warm cycles 2–5 deliver 1,780.65 aligned tokens/s and spend 14.89% of aggregate cycle time waiting for responses. This improves the earlier batch-256 result but does not establish consistently fed training. The performance track owns further admission, profiling, capacity and Snowball comparisons. Neither learning allocation remains active.

Production changes are available as draft PRs marin-community/MarinSkyRL#791–#800 alongside marin-community/MarinSkyRL#765, marin-community/MarinSkyRL#766, marin-community/MarinSkyRL#767, marin-community/MarinSkyRL#770 and marin-community/MarinSkyRL#771. Route replay is marin-community/MarinSkyRL#791; architecture marin-community/MarinSkyRL#792; publication marin-community/MarinSkyRL#793; native optimizer runtime marin-community/MarinSkyRL#794; cross-node serving marin-community/MarinSkyRL#795; restore limits marin-community/MarinSkyRL#796; async single-turn marin-community/MarinSkyRL#797; GB200 runtime marin-community/MarinSkyRL#798; vLLM runtime marin-community/MarinSkyRL#799; verifier marin-community/MarinSkyRL#800. marin-community/MarinSkyRL#793/#794 build on marin-community/MarinSkyRL#792. marin-community/MarinSkyRL#767/#770 build on marin-community/MarinSkyRL#766; marin-community/MarinSkyRL#771 builds on marin-community/MarinSkyRL#770. Land marin-community/MarinSkyRL#767 before marin-community/MarinSkyRL#794 and preserve both restore paths as shown in the combined assembly. CI is terminal and passing on every current slice head; the final check found no unresolved review threads. The [combined production tree](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/cc3d820c9f059b9d1fbfaef022a0d3a738a2682a) is `cc3d820c`; its runtime paths match validation source `f96fc755`. The combined CPU suite passes 2,060 tests, with 24 skips and two CI-prescribed deselections; the main buffer-schema followup passes 76 focused async checks, and the extracted final-line verifier passes 13 tests. The qualified GPU sources predate main’s null buffer-field declaration; each live task explicitly sets that field, and the 76 focused checks cover the schema addition. **Claude finished @ihodes's task in 1m 18s** —— [View job](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/29769915281)

---
### What #7405 delivered vs. what remains in #6503

#7405 (merged, closed #7345) built the **eval execution + reporting engine**. Mapping it against this issue's requirements:

| # | Requirement | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Run full eval list (or subset) for a checkpoint | ✅ Done | `experiments/evaluation/cli.py launch --model X --evals core\|smoke\|<subset>`. `core` = 11 lm-eval/evalchemy tasks; one serve, N evals, N durable records. |

But this is the *eval dashboard*, not yet reconciled with the public leaderboard tracked in #6043. |
| 3 | Works for our models **and** others via vLLM/OpenAI-HTTP (#4827) | ✅ Done | Demonstrated on snowball + 5 HF models; serves over the OpenAI-compatible contract; TPU (v5e→v6e→v5p sizing) and GPU (CoreWeave). |
| 4 | Defined path + **agent skill** for adding evals; evals visible on leaderboard | 🟡 Partial | README "Adding a model or eval" documents the path (`EvalSuiteConfig`→`EVALS`, `EvalModelConfig`→`MODELS`); evals are visible as dashboard columns. **No agent skill exists** (only `evaluate-zephyr-perf`, unrelated). |

### Remaining work

**1. Automated checkpoint trigger — the core gap (blocks the Definition of Done).**
The DoD is *"New checkpoint trigger → eval subset runs → results in DB → leaderboard, with zero manual steps."* #7405 provides only **manual** entry points: the `launch` CLI and a `pipeline.py` `eval_step` `ArtifactStep`. There is no code that watches for new checkpoints and auto-launches evals — no watcher/webhook/poller in `experiments/evaluation/`. This is the "Automated" in "Automated eval system" and is still entirely open. It also subsumes the open **"Trigger definition"** decision in the issue: *which* checkpoints auto-run, and *where* the trigger lives (checkpoint-export step hook, GCS-landing poll, WandB/registry event, cron sweep, etc.). The `eval_step` ArtifactStep is the natural building block — remaining work is wiring it to fire automatically.

**2. Leaderboard reconciliation (#6043).**
Evaldash exists and reads the SSOT records, but the issue asks for results on *the leaderboard* (#6043). Need to confirm whether evaldash **is** that leaderboard or whether records/DB still need to feed the #6043 surface. Likely a scope/ownership question rather than net-new plumbing.

**3. Agent skill for adding evals (requirement #4).**
Requirement #4 explicitly asks for a defined path **and an agent skill**. The README path exists; the skill does not. A `.agents/skills/add-eval/` playbook (mirroring `add-dataset`) would close this.

**4. Decision now resolved by #7405: TPU vs GPU.**
The issue flagged "TPU vs GPU, or both" as undecided — #7405 does **both** (TPU sizing heuristic + CoreWeave GPU shapes), so this decision can be marked resolved.

### Summary
#7405 nails requirements **1** and **3** and most of **2/4** (execution, multi-backend serving, durable SSOT records, a dashboard, a documented add-eval path). What remains for "Automated eval system" to be done:
- **the automatic checkpoint trigger** (biggest item; also resolves the open "Trigger definition" decision),
- **reconcile evaldash with the #6043 leaderboard**, and
- **add the `add-eval` agent skill**.

This matches @rjpower's "partly fixed in #7405" — the manual pipeline is there; the automation and leaderboard-integration layers are not yet.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
When an Iris serve job started by `marin.inference.iris.remote_inference` (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py`, `_start_direct_inference` / `_wait_for_endpoint`) is preempted by Kueue and its retry attempt registers a new endpoint on another host, the running evaluation keeps the first host:port it resolved. The Evalchemy chat client then loops on `ClientConnectorError` / `ReadTimeout` (or gets HTTP 404 from whatever now listens on that address) until the group's timeout or a manual cancel. The serve job itself is fine; only the client is stale.

Observed in marin #9920 and #9984 on cw-rno2a, 2026-10-09/10: nine evaluation groups lost this way (examples: `/karan/eval-20261009-030945-gate-rs-sft-lr1e-06-step375-5e80`, serve child `inference-553ee1e1…` preempted 6× and re-registered on 10.168.194.211 at 04:25 UTC while the eval kept 10.168.192.27:10241; `/karan/eval-20261010-030426-gate-merge-ta-a1.0-b1.0-gpqa28k-152a`, 188 logged requests answered 404 by the old address). Each costs the serve's partial GPU time plus a full relaunch; several evals ran 16–20 h before being noticed.

Expected: the client re-resolves the endpoint from the Iris registry when requests fail with connection errors (and periodically), and fails fast with a clear error when the serve job reaches a terminal state instead of retrying forever.

Done when: an eval whose serve is preempted and re-registered elsewhere continues against the new address, and an eval whose serve job dies fails within a bounded time with the serve job's state in the error.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Evalchemy launches with direct routing, and the orchestrator resolves the serve endpoint once before putting that pod address in the child job's config. The child keeps using that address while `eval_job.wait(timeout=inf)` blocks; serve health is checked only before and after the evaluation. [PR #9480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9480) chose direct routing after 7,734 hub and 10,749 peer proxy 502s in five minutes, so the recovery path must preserve direct connection reuse.

**Relevant code**
- [`launch.py#L195`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/experiments/evaluation/launch.py#L195) — selects direct Evalchemy routing
- [`runner.py#L352-L363`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L352-L363) — resolves before evaluation
- [`runner.py#L602-L609`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L602-L609) — turns registry entry into a fixed URL
- [`evalchemy/runner.py#L223-L233`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py#L223-L233) — serializes the URL into the child
- [`evalchemy/runner.py#L327`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py#L327) — waits without checking serve state

# Proposed Fix

1. Pass the endpoint name and serve job IDs to the Evalchemy child. Point Evalchemy at a loopback HTTP forwarder in that child; the forwarder uses a pooled connection to the current direct Iris endpoint and preserves streaming responses.
2. Refresh the registry address periodically and immediately after connection errors, timeouts, or a 404. Replace the upstream pool when the address changes, retry requests that have not started a response, and wait through a live job's preemption; propagate a 404 from an unchanged current address.
3. Poll serve status while the parent waits for the Evalchemy job. On a terminal serve state, cancel the evaluator and record `INFRA_FAILED` with the serve job ID and state within one poll interval; update both evaluation call paths to pass the inference session.
4. Cover address replacement, a stale-address 404, streaming interruption, recovery with no registered endpoint, and terminal serve state using local HTTP servers and a fake registry. Compare request failures and latency at Evalchemy's default concurrency before replacing direct routing.

| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Terminus-2 | **42/49 graded (85.71%)**; 1/50 ungraded; saved-answer regrade | [Regrade and provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Pi 0.87.0 | **39/46 graded (84.78%)**; 4/50 ungraded | [Run investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) |

These are **not controlled model comparisons**: benchmark variants, agents, judges, budgets, and grading policies differ. Missing submissions scored zero in both Snowball runs; the GLM rows separately report ungraded outcomes.

### Current findings

Snowball’s BixBench failures are dominated by **156 missing answer files**, plus one empty submission. Traces show answers left in chat, simulated execution without real tool calls, repetition, and specific analysis mistakes. Compaction count showed little association with missing files. BFCL also had **55/123 missing submissions**; four inspected examples show related submission/tool-use failures beyond biology, without establishing one shared cause. No scores were changed.

BiomniBench-DA likewise had **38/50 missing submissions**; the 12 submitted tasks averaged 17.67/100. Its overall 4.24/100 is a rubric-score mean, not accuracy. This supplementary evaluation used five input variants and a replacement judge/scorer; it does not change the release aggregate or provide a matched reference-model comparison. [Protocol and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6297505720).

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 The five-question GLM-5.3 BixBench CLI pilot completed with an answer from every task. The original verifier scored three answers: one correct, two incorrect, and two unscored because structured JSON generation exhausted the judge's token limit. The incomplete original run retains no aggregate metric.

A separate, uniform regrade of the same five saved answers added an explicit JSON-schema instruction to the judge. It produced one correct and four incorrect results, with no JSON errors; the three previously valid grades stayed unchanged. This is a five-question integration pilot with a disclosed judge-prompt variation, not a full-benchmark accuracy estimate. The original answers, trajectories, and scores were preserved.

The format repair is in [Harbor commit `97037f79`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800). It preserves the comparison prompt, Boolean schema, judge model, and 1,024-token cap. Lint and formatting passed. The branch has no PR yet; existing registry snapshots still require regenerated or explicitly patched tasks.

Error review:

- `bix-11-q2`: 88/249 fungal trees exceed the treeness threshold, giving 35.34%, versus the reference's 35%. The regrader rejected the difference. This is a likely precision-related false negative; no score has been changed. The pinned question specifies no rounding rule, and its archive contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-52-q2`: the agent used pooled CpGs / genome length. The [reference capsule](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) groups only chromosomes containing retained CpGs (notebook cells 11 and 39). Averaging those 20 chromosome densities yields 1.1283e-7, inside the reference interval. The notebook confirms the chromosome selection; the mean was recomputed from the saved table.
- `bix-28-q1`: the final analysis substituted raw terminal branch lengths and species-level medians for the [PhyKIT long-branch statistic](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/reference/commands/long_branch_score.html). The reference p-value has not been independently reproduced; its archive also contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-6-q7`: the agent used a top-1% replicate intersection, then mistook its own intermediate enrichment CSV for supplied results. The [reference notebook](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-f4dcda89-678d-403d-b155-1483d0071765.zip), cells 28–30, instead takes the minimum replicate P-value, selects values below 0.05, maps RefSeq IDs to symbols, and runs Reactome enrichment against measured genes. It reports “cGMP effects” with raw P ≈ 0.000024 and adjusted P ≈ 0.0327. These are saved reference outputs, not a fresh rerun.
- `bix-18-q2`: the mean swarming area was correctly rounded to 82,000.

Six additional fixed judge diagnostics accepted `35.0%` as equivalent to `35%`, rejected `45%`, and classified one value inside and one outside the CpG reference interval correctly. The exact-percent and higher-precision examples returned provider server errors, so this check did not resolve the rounding concern. No tolerance or solver setting was retuned.

The [previously documented protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5736346928) and explicit environment overrides were retained. All five pilot agents submitted within their original time limits, with no observed disk exhaustion. The full 205-question run remains pending a decision on numerical grading; original scores will remain intact.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 GLM-5.3 completed 205 fresh BixBench CLI attempts: **101 correct / 187 graded (54.01%)**, with **18 ungraded**. Grading coverage is **91.22%**. Marin's 95% interval accounting for ungraded items is **43.79–63.43%**; 54.01% is the accuracy among graded questions.

All 177 valid native grades were retained. Eleven saved answers whose verifier calls failed with HTTP 503 received one additional grading attempt each, with the original SDK retry policy. Ten obtained grades (eight correct, two incorrect); one still failed with a provider error. No solver was rerun or answer edited. The original run and its artifacts remain preserved.

The 18 ungraded outcomes are:

- 14 missing answer/reward files following the 3,600-second agent limit.
- Two sandbox processes killed with exit 137 (`TmuxBatchProtocolError`); the cause is unconfirmed.
- One Daytona HTTP 502 gateway failure.
- One unresolved judge server error (`bix-10-q2`).

Three other trials reported `AgentTimeoutError` but produced valid verifier results; those grades remain included. Missing grades are excluded from the accuracy denominator and shown separately. The original private exporter mistakenly required 100% grading coverage; its incomplete record is preserved. The derived result applies [Marin's standard 90% completion gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py), consistent with the reporting policy in #9193. The original sample export displayed missing rewards as incorrect; the derived archive preserves all 18 as ungraded.

Protocol: `bixbench-cli@1.5`, Harbor `7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a`, task revision `711ff277ae6b9e3950d19b40bc3e5aeb96e62b73`, Terminus-2, 16 concurrent trials, 32,768 input / 8,192 output tokens, default summarization, and 3,600-second agent / 600-second verifier limits. The judge was Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b` with the original comparison prompt and 1,024-token cap. The [explicit JSON-schema repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800) applied to every task; numerical tolerances were unchanged. The [previously documented](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5742640265) 10 GiB disk override, pinned AMD64 image, and task-manifest hash were retained.

Validation checked all 205 task identities, sample counts against aggregate scores, all retained native grades, and the eleven selected recovery cases. Two archived trajectories were also compared byte-for-byte through the dashboard API. This establishes an exploratory CLI baseline; ID/OOD status remains unassigned. The replacement judge, missing grades, known precision caveat from the pilot, and unavailable exact serving weights revision limit comparisons with other protocols. Next: review full-run scientific errors and compare future models under this same recorded protocol.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Reviewed all 86 recorded incorrect answers and all 18 ungraded outcomes from the [completed BixBench CLI baseline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667), using saved answers/trajectories and the archived reference notebooks where available. No solver or judge calls were rerun. The result remains **101/187 correct (54.01%), with 18/205 ungraded**.

Each incorrect answer has a primary review category:

| Category | Questions | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Observed analysis or protocol divergence | 54 | Identified differences in statistic, counting unit, filtering, cohort, model or enrichment workflow. Some choices are underspecified in the question; these are not all established scientific mistakes. |
| Answer precision or representation review | 11 | Submitted values may differ through rounding or units; this does not establish 11 false negatives. |
| Question or reference adjudication | 7 | Contradictory targets, unclear counting/aggregation, or unresolved reference-data provenance. |
| Numerical or pipeline mismatch unresolved | 14 | Insufficient evidence to isolate the cause without reconstructing more of the reference pipeline. |

The review ledger records a finding, confidence level, trace evidence and pinned reference capsule for each of the 104 nonpassing outcomes. Original trajectories remain in the existing evaluation archive; the detailed review ledger is retained with the private evaluation handoff. The categories above are follow-up queues, not a corrected accuracy estimate.

Concrete analysis findings:

- `bix-61-q1`: reported **4,818 discarded read pairs across two samples**. The MDR trimming log reconstructs the reference's **344,895 discarded individual reads** exactly: 334,988 forward-only survivors + 1,075 reverse-only survivors + 2 × 4,416 fully dropped pairs. Both the counting unit and sample scope changed.
- `bix-28-q4` and `bix-45-q5`: substituted a different statistic. The former used terminal-branch means grouped by species instead of per-tree long-branch scores; the latter used BUSCO score/cutoff instead of [PhyKIT relative composition variability](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/tutorials/pages/01-summarizing-information-content.html).
- `bix-16-q1/q3`: raw Chronos scores were used without the reference's sign reversal. `bix-20-q1/q3`: unclassified variants entered the denominator; the reference excludes them, giving 13/14 and 35/37. These differences are visible in the [essentiality reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-bda54b38-9b49-4009-aad6-d5f52675438a.zip), cell 34, and [variant reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-2ccdbe37-0a92-47b5-9bab-fa8a8c470799.zip), cell 18.
- RNA-seq failures repeatedly differed in count normalization, outlier exclusion, covariates, nominal versus adjusted p-values, enrichment gene lists and background. For example, the [JBX13 reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-1d54e4a7-8b0f-4224-bd31-efcfded0d46c.zip) removes three samples and models replicate, strain and medium; several answers retained all samples and omitted replicate. The [UBE2M reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) removes KL3/WL3 before enrichment, unlike the `bix-53-q6` answer. Exact contributions were not isolated through reruns.
- `bix-10` / `bix-29` severity questions also expose a reference-definition caveat: the [reference preprocessing](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-fbe0e950-76f2-4eb7-a216-a2d377970922.zip), cell 17, aggregates all adverse events per participant, although questions call the endpoint COVID severity. COVID-specific/event-level alternatives therefore need protocol adjudication.

Grading and reference findings:

- `bix-19-q2` is a calculation-versus-submission example: the agent computed **Cohen's d = 0.216284**, independently matching [reference cell 30](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-8c64b1fa-fdcc-41e2-be8d-2f0c8d5faaa1.zip), but submitted approximately **0.22**. That final answer falls outside the target interval **0.215–0.217**. Other precision candidates include 35.34% versus 35% and 5.23 versus 5.2. The 11 cases are `4-q1/q5/q6`, `11-q1/q2/q5`, `19-q2`, `28-q6`, `38-q1/q3`, and `54-q5`, all with prefix `bix-`. Tiny nonzero p-values are not automatically equivalent to literal zero; `54-q5` also has a model-input difference alongside its ratio/fraction representation.
- `bix-53-q4` has a confirmed malformed target: the question requests a **pathway count**, but the [original ideal answer](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/BixBench.jsonl) is **4.25E-04**. [Reference cell 79](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) explicitly counts **2** pathways. The submitted answer was **1**, so fixing the target would not automatically make it correct.
- `bix-31-q2` contradicts its stated analysis. The target interval **−0.45 to −0.35** conflicts with **abs(LFC)>0.5**. [Reference cells 32–38](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-b1dbace7-f6e9-42ec-81e1-bcc24161cc27.zip) show FAM138A at baseMean **0.483698**, unshrunk LFC **−0.383938**, and shrunk LFC **−0.060666**. The target matches the unshrunk, low-expression row despite instructions requiring shrinkage and baseMean>10. The agent answered `NA`.
- `bix-52-q1` has a reference-data bug: [reference cell 14](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) downloads **JD_Chromosome_Length.csv** into **ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv**. The agent's **1.52** ratio is internally consistent with the supplied lengths and site counts; the provenance of the target **0.47–0.67** remains unresolved. `bix-52-q5` also counts repeated records instead of distinct sites, so this data caveat does not explain all CpG failures.
- The remaining four primary adjudication cases are `bix-8-q6` (260 unique genes versus 680 transcript records; [reference cell 21](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-48a6b469-9c9d-4bef-b5b4-f29b7d6fa046.zip) counts rows), `bix-38-q6` (median of paired ratios versus ratio of group medians), `bix-43-q4` (8/514 DE genes versus 8/49 pathway genes), and `bix-22-q6` (the origin of the 0.3–0.4 correlation target was not established). These require explicit definitions or reference reconstruction.
- `bix-54-q4` additionally has reversed target interval bounds, but its submitted p-value lies outside even the sorted interval. This metadata defect does not rescue that answer.

The [verifier](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py) asks an LLM for binary equivalence. It has **no separate global numerical-tolerance rule**; some targets contain explicit intervals. The JSON-schema repair changes response format, not this comparison prompt. Before any rescoring, define a consistent precision/adjudication policy and preserve the present native grades as a separate baseline.

The 14 missing-answer traces show long model fits, repeated workbook inspection, unresolved analysis choices, and sensitivity checks after intermediate results existed. More time alone is not a demonstrated fix. The two exit-137 cases show killed statistical processes; excessive worker creation is a plausible contributor, but an OOM cause is unconfirmed. One gateway failure and `bix-10-q2`'s persistent judge 503 remain ungraded. The latter has a saved answer outside its target interval, but no manual grade was substituted.

Next: adjudicate the flagged question/reference and precision cases; document the intended analysis protocols; then select a small set of failures for any separately approved controlled rerun. Keep any revised scoring or solver results separate from this baseline. The existing verifier JSON-format PR follow-up remains open.

Reference links above use dataset revision `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; notebook cell indices are zero-based. Several phylogenetic and genomic-pipeline capsules contain no reference notebook, which limits causal conclusions for the 14 unresolved cases.

comments.body:
🤖 Agent-runtime summary for the [completed 205-question BixBench CLI run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667). Measured from each original Harbor trial’s `agent_execution.started_at` and `finished_at`; all 205 have both timestamps.

The median agent runtime was **5.6 minutes per question**. The middle 50% took **1.7–15.5 minutes**, and the 90th percentile was **37.3 minutes**.

| Questions | n | Median, min | 25th–75th percentile, min | 90th percentile, min | Mean, min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All attempted questions | 205 | 5.6 | 1.7–15.5 | 37.3 | 12.8 |
| Solver completed without interruption | 185 | 4.7 | 1.6–13.8 | 20.5 | 8.6 |
| Final grade: correct | 101 | 2.3 | 0.9–9.2 | 17.3 | 6.9 |
| Final grade: incorrect | 86 | 8.1 | 2.8–14.8 | 26.5 | 12.3 |

These are elapsed solving times, including model responses, command execution, waits and tool/network latency during the agent phase. They exclude separately timed sandbox setup, agent setup and grading. Quantiles use linear interpolation at `(n−1)×p`.

**17/205 tasks (8.3%) reached the configured 3,600-second agent cap**: 14 had no submitted answer and remained ungraded; 3 retained gradeable answers. The other three interrupted agents had two process-kill failures and one gateway failure. Capped times measure time spent before termination, not the uncensored time required to solve those tasks. Recorded capped durations were 3,600.0–3,602.3 seconds.

The median complete trial duration, including setup, grading and teardown, was **7.3 minutes**. The interval from the first trial start to the last trial finish was **3 h 28 min 48 s**.

The 185 uninterrupted solver completions include one answer whose judge still failed. Correct/incorrect rows use final saved-answer recovery grades and retain the three scored timeouts. Runtime differences between outcome groups are descriptive; task difficulty and workflow differences confound interpretation.

The complete launcher-to-export span was **3 h 36 min 11 s**, with a cap of **16 concurrent trials**. That batch span includes setup and final export; later saved-answer judge recovery is excluded. The [existing result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) remains 101/187 correct with 18 ungraded.

Per-question times, raw timestamps, source hashes and the summary calculation are retained in the private evaluation handoff. No new evaluation or grading calls were made.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Completed the 18-case BixBench adjudication review. Five cases have confirmed task/reference defects; nine are candidates for accepting equivalent numerical presentations (one retains an analysis-method caveat); one is an actual submitted-answer precision error; three remain unresolved because the reference precision or analysis specification is insufficient. **Original grades remain 101/187 across 205 attempts.** No solver or judge calls were made.

The decision policy evaluates the submitted answer, respects explicit target intervals, keeps integer counts exact, and permits only justified unit/ratio conversions. Eight cases are equivalent when rounded to the reference's displayed precision, but that is a review criterion, not an adopted universal scoring rule. Zero-valued p-value targets require an explicit threshold or precision rule. A defective task does not automatically make its submitted answer correct.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

These are 617 distinct transcript IDs, so 680 is a row count, not even a unique-transcript count. The reference count(m6A) counts rows; the submitted 260 matches unique genes having at least one hypermethylated record. | Prefer explicitly asking for unique gene_id values with at least one hypermethylated record and setting the count to 260. The submitted difference 0.05014 rounds to 0.05. The other numbers in the answer describe its two operands. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-11-q2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-cd811ead-7887-4369-b175-05aff4223765.zip) | 35.34% → 35% | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 35.34% rounds to 35%; saved calculation is 88/249 = 35.3414%. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-11-q5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-cd811ead-7887-4369-b175-05aff4223765.zip) | p = 2.0944e-26 → 0.0 | **Unresolved reference precision**. Submitted Mann–Whitney p = 2.0944e-26; saved two-sided asymptotic calculation gives U = 3556 and p = 2.0944031684e-26. The ideal 0.0 contains no usable significance threshold or numerical tolerance. No original reference notebook was available for this capsule. | Ask for a nonzero reference p-value with documented test options, or an explicit threshold/rounding instruction. Do not infer that every small p-value is equivalent to zero. |
| [bix-19-q2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-8c64b1fa-fdcc-41e2-be8d-2f0c8d5faaa1.zip) | Cohen's d ≈ 0.22 (KD − CTRL mean difference = 3.875 NeuN; pooled SD) → Between 0.215 and 0.217 inclusive | **Submitted-answer precision error**. Both the saved calculation and notebook give Cohen's d = 0.2162844172. The actual submission says approximately 0.22, outside the explicit 0.215–0.217 reference interval. | Retain incorrect under the existing interval. Do not replace a submitted answer with a better number from the trajectory. Future instructions should state the required precision. |
| [bix-22-q6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-34a4ea96-c800-4c11-959e-57cdc4932c52.zip) | 0.0504 → Between 0.3 and 0.4 inclusive | **Unresolved analysis specification**. Streaming the 106 MB count matrix reproduces the agent's 0.05038279 for 19,942 protein-coding genes over all 723 samples. Reproducing notebook filtering (exclude PBMC, protein_coding substring, immune total >=10) yields 17,819 genes over 565 samples, pooled correlation 0.03865223, and CD4/CD8/CD14/CD19 correlations 0.04988913/0.04367048/0.02052692/0.03566210, matching notebook outputs. None supports target 0.3–0.4. | Specify sample set, gene filter, expression summary and whether correlation is pooled or cell-type specific; regenerate the reference from that pipeline. A factor-of-ten typo is plausible but not established, and the agent and notebook use different cohorts. |
| [bix-28-q6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-c66d3ed9-0a95-46be-a237-ed68498ea7f6.zip) | 5.23 → 5.2 | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 5.23 rounds to 5.2; saved calculation is 5.2282463. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-31-q2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-b1dbace7-f6e9-42ec-81e1-bcc24161cc27.zip) | NA → Between -0.45 and -0.35 inclusive | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. The capsule annotation identifies FAM138A as lncRNA. Notebook cell 26 fits batch + sex; cell 32 gives baseMean 0.483698 and unshrunk LFC -0.383938; cell 36 gives shrunk LFC -0.060666. The target -0.45 to -0.35 matches the unshrunk row, contradicting the protein-coding, baseMean >10, abs(LFC)>0.5 and shrinkage requirements. NA is defensible for exclusion. | Minimal repair: explicitly ask for the unshrunk FAM138A sex coefficient from the batch + sex model before those filters. Alternatively retain the intended filtered/shrunken task and choose an eligible gene with a regenerated target. |
| [bix-38-q1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-975f3e91-53b0-44b1-ac9f-20023d9c8cd0.zip) | 2.18-fold (fungi / animals) → 2x larger in fungi | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 2.18-fold agrees with the coarse 2x target. Recomputed ratio of full-precision group medians is 2.177433; ratio of rounded IQ-TREE report medians is 2.177509. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-38-q3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-975f3e91-53b0-44b1-ac9f-20023d9c8cd0.zip) | 5.22% → 5% | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 5.22% rounds to 5%; saved calculation is 13/249 = 5.2209%. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-38-q6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-975f3e91-53b0-44b1-ac9f-20023d9c8cd0.zip) | 1.9036 → 2.178 | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. Independent Newick branch-length sums find 96 paired orthologs and median(fungal_length/animal_length) = 1.9036165971, matching the submission. The target 2.178 instead matches the ratio of separately rounded group medians, 3.0962/1.4219 = 2.1775089669; that uses all 249 fungal and 100 animal trees. Full-precision group medians give 2.177433, also a different estimand. | Keep the paired-ratio question; reference 1.9036165971 with a declared tolerance, or explicitly request 1.904 to three decimal places. Preserve the paired ortholog list and full-precision input calculation. |
| [bix-43-q4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-15ff11e5-2db1-45b6-b3a3-46bc2a74b821.zip) | 8/514 → 8/49 | **Unresolved analysis specification**. The prompt asks for the proportion of differentially expressed genes, but reference cell 65 reports the Enrichr overlap 8/49, whose denominator is pathway members. Agent 8/514 uses its DEG denominator. The notebook has 679 pre-mapping DEG rows at cell 45 and drops missing gene names at cell 53; the final distinct mapped denominator was not established. | Minimal repair: ask for the Enrichr Overlap field, explicitly defined as intersecting genes / pathway genes, and retain 8/49. If retaining the DEG-proportion wording, establish mapping/deduplication and recompute that denominator. Do not certify 514 as the reference count. |
| [bix-52-q1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) | Chromosome W / chromosome 1 = 1.52 → Between 0.47 and 0.67 inclusive | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. Packaged ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv is byte-identical to JD_Chromosome_Length.csv (SHA256 59e321ef…051b); notebook cell 14 downloads the JD file under the ZF name. Three W and 29 chr1 distinct filtered sites give 1.519930 with that supplied table. The original Zenodo ZF table gives W length 20,846,394 and chr1 length 114,020,016, yielding 0.56581364, inside the existing 0.47–0.67 interval. | Replace the mislabeled capsule asset and notebook download URL with the original ZF table (Zenodo record 12205202, MD5 b078a4dab5b677bfd0742452de6b1a17). Retain the existing target interval. Future evaluation needs the corrected input; do not retroactively penalize the agent for using the supplied file. |
| [bix-53-q4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) | 1 → 4.25E-04 | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. The original dataset ideal is 4.25E-04 for a question asking how many pathways. Notebook cell 79 explicitly counts two oxidative terms among the top twenty. The submitted one is not correct merely because the gold is malformed. | Use integer target 2 only with the notebook's intended cohort, adjusted-p filtering, shrinkage and pathway-term matching explicitly specified. The current question says p while the notebook filters padj; pin that distinction before a corrected task is released. |
| [bix-54-q5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-9e52daf6-ca58-43e8-e732-fbac3459d295.zip) | 10:1 → Between 0.9 and 0.99 inclusive | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 10:1 converts to a component fraction 10/11 = 0.90909, inside 0.90–0.99. Reference cells 16/19 use rhlI/(rhlI+lasI) and yield a spline maximum at 0.9076577. The prompt asks for a ratio but the target stores a fraction. The agent selected the best tested ratio from 36 mixed-culture rows; the reference spline used 39 rows, so final-answer equivalence does not validate the method. | State that the answer is the rhlI fraction; allow an explicitly labeled equivalent mixture ratio if retaining outcome-only grading. Keep the method caveat separate. |

Evidence uses the pinned BixBench dataset `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; task links above point to the corresponding source capsule. Notebook cell numbers are zero-based. Local reproduction records include the downloaded-member SHA256 manifest, gene/correlation checks, and all 96 paired tree ratios. The corrected Zebra Finch file is available in [the original Zenodo dataset](https://zenodo.org/records/12205202).

A separate [public BixBench audit](https://github.com/Anqi-Dai/BixBench_eval/blob/6070dc293677b0ef21fa38d7ab23c5850d8799c0/env/REVIEW_REPORT.md) independently documents the 680-record/260-gene mismatch. Its study covers three capsules and fourteen questions; it does not validate this entire run.

The proposed precision rule was also screened against **all 205 saved outcomes, including the 101 previously correct answers**. This was a conservative scalar/range screen, not a complete semantic regrade: 81 answers require semantic parsing, and counts, unit conversions, reversed ranges and the zero p-value need explicit treatment. It flags two existing passes that a naive comparator would reject: `bix-18-q5` supplies 0.29 against a percent-scale 25–30 target, and `bix-45-q1` supplies 7.70e-54 against 7.6968e-54. The latter needs symmetric handling of reported precision, rather than always requiring the target's extra digits. These findings block adopting a blanket rounding rule or publishing a selectively corrected accuracy.

Harbor Index provides relevant prior work: its public index includes five BixBench-derived tasks, with eighteen trials each. [Its Jackdaw notes](https://hub.harborframework.com/tasks/harbor-index/bix-cpg-density-jackdaw/latest) explicitly say the scientific derivation was not re-audited. Later [PR #142](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/pull/142) fixed underspecified instructions for two tasks present in this run: miRNA analysis `bix-30-q1` ([issue #97](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/issues/97)) and ordinal regression `bix-10-q2` ([issue #113](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/issues/113)). The fixes specify preprocessing/modeling choices while retaining the targets. These are useful precedents for task repair, not grounds for changing our recorded grades. The index uses its own 1,200-second budgets and deterministic numeric verifiers; its results are not directly comparable to this baseline.

Next: review the seven local upstream-report drafts; agree on versioned task repairs and numerical tolerances; then validate any revised grader across all 205 outcomes before publishing a separate result. The fourteen other numerical/pipeline discrepancies and ungraded outcomes remain follow-ups. The main issue table records **per-question agent time**, with no total-duration column.

comments.body:
🤖 The pilot is idle with no GPU jobs running. Both planned 10-step attempts stopped in tiny-model preflight before student loading. Working Snowball SFT precedents now include a report on the same September 21 checkpoint, but the exact training path is not yet matched to this pilot. Resume after obtaining a reproducible working revision/configuration and reviewing the remaining differences. The baseline remains 0/1; the earlier four-step model’s incoherent evaluation remains ungraded.

<details>
<summary>Checkpoint, smoke findings, and next steps (September 23, 2026)</summary>

- **Hold further GPU runs; closer precedent identified (September 23):** The user supplied the text of [Harshit Varma’s report](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1374989195109466122/1552425627976474645). It continues the same `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21` checkpoint on filtered AgentTrove plus GLM-5.3 RST successes: 63,504 rows, two epochs/722 steps, batch 64, sequence 32,768, `5e-5` AdamH with cosine and 3% warmup. Reported held-out NLL improves 1.094 → 0.909 and parse-fail turns fall 67% → 25%, while premature completion, recovery, and long-context behavior regress. This supports a functioning SFT/serving path for our student, not a claim of improved overall TB2 performance. The screenshot does not give hardware, code revision, or the exact optimizer class.

  The completed four-step biology pilot used ordinary Adam at constant `5e-5`; the unexecuted ten-step plan uses ordinary Adam with cosine and no warmup. [Marin’s AdamH implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045/lib/levanter/src/levanter/optim/adamh.py) preserves matrix norms and uses separate parameter groups, so equal nominal learning rates do not imply equivalent updates. This is a material difference to review, not an established explanation for the earlier incoherent model or the preflight NaNs. The latter occurred before any optimizer update.

  [Luke’s pinned launch record](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/d152f86a58e8619a988361e1502f9e55) is a separate reproducible precedent: `lukedhlee/vista-snowball-sft@23d8fda7`, Grug trainer/AdamH, 16 × 4 GH200s, EP8, batch 64, sequence 32,768, and a different Stage-3 starting model. It cannot be substituted for Harshit’s unspecified setup without checking those differences. Further GPU submissions are on hold with the user’s agreement; preserve the 31 traces, baseline, and failed-run evidence. The resume condition is an exact successful training/export configuration, not a merge flag alone.

- **Working precedents and revised recommendation (September 23, 21:15 UTC):** [PR #9331](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9331) reports completed one-update Snowball SFT followed by FinanceBench evaluation: baseline 26/50, task-only 27/50, curriculum 23/50. Those results use an earlier unpacked, assistant-masked path; the PR explicitly distinguishes the later packed/full-text recipe, which has not been rerun on H100s. [Issue #9380](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9380) separately documents a 64-H100 run at step 135 with a usable HF export despite a final checkpoint rewrite error. Our two failed preflights establish a problem in the tested configuration, not a general Snowball SFT blocker. The next investigation should recover and compare a successful run’s exact revision, model, mesh, attention backend, and data path before proposing another allocation. #9328 [merged into the #9331 feature branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9328#issuecomment-5802057836), so its merged flag does not establish a new validated main-branch recipe. The Discord message was subsequently supplied as a screenshot; its report is summarized above. No additional GPU run was submitted.

- **Corrected GPU preflight failed (September 23, 19:28 UTC):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-layoutfix-20260923-192616` passed the previous incompatible-sharding operation, then failed the strict native/previous gradient comparison with `AssertionError: (nan, nan)`. The recorded reference-gradient magnitude is NaN; the current logging does not identify the first affected parameter or establish whether the native gradient is also non-finite. CPU testing used reference attention; this GPU preflight uses `gpu_fa4_cute`, context parallelism, and a different tiny shape. The cause is unresolved, and this does not establish a failure of the 10-step schedule or the full student. **Zero student updates, no new trained checkpoint, all four GPU tasks terminal.** No tolerances were relaxed and no further GPU retry was submitted. Recommendation: resume after a maintainer-tested H100 forward/backward and usable HF-export path is available, then repeat preflight before training. Merge status alone does not establish those checks. Keep the 31 accepted traces, matched baseline, and agreed hyperparameters for that retry.

- **Corrected retry submitted (September 23, 19:26 UTC):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-layoutfix-20260923-192616` uses pinned `ca9511b` plus the CPU-tested one-line layout correction described below. Output is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-cosine10-native-loss-layoutfix-20260923/`. The launcher verifies the original and patched source SHA256 before importing the model. Training remains ten cosine steps from `5e-5`, batch eight, length 4,096, fresh optimizer, and final BF16 export only, with zero automatic retries and a 75-minute cap. The matched original-task evaluation is prepared; 21 protocol fields and the task archive hash match the baseline. Evaluation waits for verified training/export completion.

- **CPU reproduction and candidate correction passed (September 23):** `/exedev/bio-native-loss-cpu-repro-20260923-191828` reproduced the exact native-loss `ShardingTypeError` using a tiny random Snowball model and 32 virtual CPU devices. Wrapping the per-token loss with `hax.auto_sharded(...)` before the existing weighted reduction resolved it. Against the preceding pilot loss, FP32 losses were **3.874972582 vs 3.874972820**, with maximum absolute gradient difference **2.24e-8**; BF16 loss and gradients matched exactly. Tolerances remain `atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5`. This checks a targeted layout correction, not full-model GPU or generation correctness. The original GPU preflight remains required. A retry is prepared with the same 10 cosine steps, batch eight, sequence 4,096, original checkpoint, 32 H100s, and final export only. This adds one documented native-code correction to pinned `ca9511b`; The approved GPU retry is recorded above.

- **Native-loss preflight failed (September 23, 19:12 UTC):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-20260923-191030` reached `loading_preflight → native_value_grad → Snowball.compute_next_token_loss → maybe_reduce_loss`, then raised `ShardingTypeError` at `arr * effective_weight`. The loss uses `((replica_dcn, data, expert), context)`; the mask uses `((replica_dcn, replica, data), None)`. Source: [Snowball loss at the tested revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py#L838). This occurred on the tiny random model before student loading: **zero student updates and no new trained checkpoint**. All four GPU tasks are terminal. The 10-step cosine hypothesis remains untested. CPU-only job `/exedev/bio-native-loss-cpu-repro-20260923-191828` completed the failure reproduction and correction checks described above. It uses no pretrained weights and has a ten-minute cap. The approved GPU retry is recorded above.

- **Agreed experiment submitted (September 23, 19:10 UTC):** job `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-20260923-191030` restarts from the original September 21 checkpoint with **10 updates, cosine decay from 5e-5, global batch eight, sequence 4,096, no packing**, and the native recipe's Adam settings. Eighty presentations are about 2.58 passes over 31 traces. The full conversations average 2,822 tokens and have a maximum of 3,477, so 4,096 preserves all examples. Use [PR #9328 at `ca9511b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045) for Snowball's native loss; the PR remains unmerged. The documented exceptions are the existing BF16 CPU import/native GPU placement helper and a thin Trainer driver with default checkpoint hooks disabled. This preserves the agreed final-BF16-export-only policy; the stock launcher would force a model-and-optimizer checkpoint. Distributed initialization precedes model config parsing; W&B and reference-code copying remain disabled. A tiny native/previous loss-and-gradient comparison, exact checkpoint round trip, and an 80-presentation corpus audit precede student loading. The same first training batch will be scored before and after each update; it remains training data and creates no validation split. Use 32 H100s with zero retries and the existing 75-minute cap. A newer maintainer-tested path can be tried when available.

- **Full regression audit completed (September 23):** CPU-only job `/exedev/bio-sft-weight-audit-20260923-183344` compared **67,078,882,816 values across 502 tensors and 39 shards**. Both checkpoints have zero non-finite values; no delta exceeds the conservative four-update Adam bound plus BF16 rounding. Global relative L2 change is **0.414%**. This reduces evidence for gross corruption but does not rule out harmful optimization or training semantics. Source/final tokenizer JSON, inference/training templates, and generation configuration match exactly. Full per-tensor report: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-sft-weight-audit-20260923-183344/report.json`.

- **Post-SFT evaluation stopped and preserved (September 23, 18:20 UTC):** `/exedev/snowball-sep21-bix51-post-sft-20260923-180511` produced incoherent, invalid JSON from its first response; later inspected responses remained incoherent. Harbor received SIGINT after approval and saved the trial as `CancelledError`: one attempted, zero graded, no answer, null reward, **496.04 seconds** of agent execution. This is not a scored benchmark failure. The parent is terminal and its eight-H100 inference child was released. A subsequent Daytona inventory found no owned sandbox. Canonical record: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-sep21-bix51-post-sft-20260923-180511/record.json`; sibling `results/protocol-stop.json` records the stop. Trajectory SHA256: `93b4bb468d4b09ad466903809711b01b0a6e1507009f51d5b42b770f99321c0f`.

- **Regression investigation:** sixteen evaluation settings and all task-file hashes match the coherent baseline. The tiny HF round-trip check and finite training losses do not establish full-model generation correctness after updates. The [native recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2163b2b4e50bdeb697f17433e296ad9fe842008f/experiments/sft/configs/snowball_h100.py) uses a base checkpoint, ten updates, and cosine decay from `5e-5`; this pilot continued an SFT checkpoint for four updates at constant `5e-5`. Those settings are not validated for this continuation. Too few updates may limit learning; an excessive learning rate, training error, or export/serving mismatch could explain the degradation. The completed weight audit and the subsequent cosine run are recorded above.

- **SFT and final export succeeded (September 23):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-native32h-20260923-174000` completed successfully on all four tasks. Its loader audit confirms **31 unique traces presented once**, four updates, one zero-loss padding slot, **26,963 supervised tokens**, and exclusion of the original task. Full-weight training used FP32 parameters/Adam, BF16 compute, batch eight, sequence 4,096, and learning rate 5e-5. Final export contains **39 shards and 502 tensors**, with **134,157,765,632 bytes of BF16 tensor data**; the complete index matches the source tensor names, total tensor bytes, and shard mapping. No optimizer or intermediate checkpoint was saved. Rank-zero timings: **154.36 seconds** to import/place/cast the student, **33.39 seconds** for the four updates, and **984.66 seconds (16.4 minutes)** for export. All updates had finite loss. This successful attempt used **11.45 recorded GPU-hours**; the eight native 32-GPU attempts total **43.30 GPU-hours**, excluding earlier eight-GPU experiments and the new evaluation. These are task-runtime figures, not a provider bill.

- **Trained artifact and evaluation:** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-1epoch-32h100-fixedio-20260923/hf/`; sibling `training-complete.json` records the audit, losses, timings, tensor count, and index SHA256. The matched evaluation `/exedev/snowball-sep21-bix51-post-sft-20260923-180511` was submitted at 18:05 UTC for **one attempt on unchanged `bix-51-q2`**, using eight H100s and the baseline's `/nothink` protocol. It checks the saved training-completion record, index, shard presence, and inference template before serving. Sixteen protocol fields and all task-file hashes match the baseline. The result is pending; this one-task test will not establish a benchmark-wide score or pass-rate estimate.

- **Preceding attempt stopped before student loading (September 23):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-native32g-20260923-171659` passed the tiny GPU-cast/import/export check: one finite optimizer update and all 103 BF16 HF tensors exactly preserved. The new I/O probe then failed because `get_fs_token_paths(..., mode="wb")` expands a scalar destination into `io-probe.safetensors/0.part`, while verification and cleanup targeted the parent as a file. This is a bug in the pilot probe. The corrected call uses `expand=False` and asserts the exact destination; a local file write/read/delete regression passed. No real student weights loaded in that failed attempt; the corrected retry is recorded above. All four tasks ended at 17:21:16 UTC, using **2.15 recorded GPU-hours**; the seven native 32-GPU attempts total **31.85 GPU-hours**, excluding earlier eight-GPU experiments. The corrected retry subsequently removed the probe's temporary `0.part` object. Provenance: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-1epoch-32h100-gpucast-20260923/provenance/`.

- **Upstream SFT findings checked (September 23):** [PR #9316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9316) is already the pilot's source revision. The newly reported failures have concrete scope: [#9372](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9372) initializes JAX during HF config parsing; the pilot initializes distributed JAX first. [#9373](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9373) concerns CUDA/NCCL setup; the pilot's distributed optimizer and compilation checks passed. [#9375](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9375) concerns W&B startup; the pilot disables W&B. [#9377](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9377) fails while copying reference code from S3; the pilot already uses `save_reference_code=False` and validates final metadata. [#9380](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9380) rewrites a saved final TensorStore checkpoint on resume; the pilot saves no TensorStore checkpoints and does not resume one. The reported 64-H100 run completed its HF export, although Iris marked that resume failed during final checkpoint writing. This does not establish a 64-GPU requirement for the shorter pilot, which already completed four updates on 32 H100s at sequence length 4,096.

- **CPU I/O measurement:** the prior CPU-only regional benchmark uploaded an existing 3,431,580,288-byte shard in **13.70 seconds with the native uploader**, versus **27.14 seconds with fsutil streaming**. Both full readbacks matched the source MD5, and both temporary copies were removed. Keep the native exporter. This does not explain the earlier slower H100-worker export. The current recovery retains the 45-second training-node upload gate and 75-minute cap; the corrected run completed full-model import and final export, with timings recorded above.

- **Training ran; export timed out (September 23):** the September 21 student completed all four planned full-weight SFT updates on **32 H100s**, using the 31 accepted traces once, FP32 parameters/Adam, BF16 compute, and no intermediate checkpoints. All four ranks logged update 4 with finite loss **1.2927228**. The first update took **303.7 seconds including compilation**; later retained update timings were **1.5–1.8 seconds**. These are different batches, so the losses do not establish improvement. The job then exceeded its 45-minute task cap during the final 39-shard HF export. At the last object inventory, five completed shards were present; the export is incomplete and unusable, and **post-SFT evaluation has not run**. All four GPU tasks are terminal. Recorded runtime was **24.27 GPU-hours** for this attempt and **29.70 GPU-hours across today's six native 32-GPU attempts**; this excludes earlier eight-GPU experiments and is task-runtime accounting, not a provider bill.

- **Remaining blocker:** checkpoint I/O dominates this short pilot. A stack captured the import callback converting BF16 to FP32 on the CPU; export logs show slow sequential shard uploads. A later CPU profile did not establish a single upload bottleneck. The preceding retry stopped in the probe path bug above. The corrected run subsequently completed import, training, and final export as recorded above. Resolve and measure the I/O path before another full attempt, then run the already prepared matched `/nothink` evaluation on unchanged `bix-51-q2`. The partial output stays under the existing `ttl=14d` prefix and must not be treated as a completed checkpoint.

- **Distributed preflight passed (September 23):** on four nodes / 32 H100s, a tiny Snowball completed one optimizer update with finite loss **5.5434394**. The launcher pins Python 3.12, includes Iris's CUDA 13 setup, and uses the shared path required by the rank-zero-only exporter. No numerical tolerance was relaxed. Source remains `2163b2b4e50bdeb697f17433e296ad9fe842008f`; task scripts and plan are saved under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-1epoch-32h100-20260923/provenance/`.

- Compatibility checks before SFT: the cached tokenizer JSON differs from September 21 in its added-token table. A CPU audit verified **identical input IDs and assistant masks on all 31 traces**, so the existing cache is retained. Training and final export now load the September 21 tokenizer explicitly. The mesh is eight expert shards within each node and four context shards across nodes. Two preceding attempts stopped before reading student weights (mesh validation, then the tokenizer-file equality guard); all their GPU tasks are terminal, with **1.27 recorded GPU-hours** in total. The current job rechecks the cache against the selected tokenizer before loading weights. No post-SFT task grade is available yet.

- Hardware decision (September 23): target **32 H100s (four nodes)** with the [native Snowball recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2163b2b4e50bdeb697f17433e296ad9fe842008f/experiments/sft/configs/snowball_h100.py), FP32 parameters/Adam state, BF16 compute, and context=4/expert=8. No student weights were loaded by that probe. Current attempt: `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-native32f-20260923-155632`. The 32-H100 job passed tiny distributed training/import/export and completed **one epoch, four updates** using the existing regional September 21 checkpoint.
